claims.statement: Verified fact: Poland's deposit system is decentralized with multiple operators, and operator-retailer contracts must address deposit settlement and packaging collection rules.
Verified fact: the Ministry reported about 2.3 billion returned containers through May 2026, with 87% returned via machines at 14,000 locations.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): multi-operator rules and transaction volume create enough recurring discrepancies to support an independent paid assurance layer.

contrary_evidence: Official guidance says each operator may design its own detailed operating and settlement rules, which may favor vertically integrated tools rather than a neutral layer: https://www.gov.pl/attachment/4369df4f-aa6a-43a4-b46d-01689735fb14
The system is already operating at very large scale, so entering after core infrastructure deployment may make integration harder: https://www.gov.pl/web/klimat/system-kaucyjny

economics.acquisition_route: Start with one producer or 20-100-store regional chain affected by multiple operators, then distribute through RVM and compliance partners.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 5 customers at PLN 8,000 MRR in year 2, 20 at PLN 12,000 MRR in year 4, and 35 at PLN 14,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 5.88m ARR before usage fees. At 20-30% owner earnings or a 3x ARR value and 65% ownership, the PLN 5m founder-net-worth mark is plausible in years 5-7; inability to standardize a second operator feed is a kill condition.
economics.founder_time: 4-5 hours/day for one design partner; cap concurrent integrations and contract a retail-data engineer after paid validation.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 68-82% gross margin once feeds stabilize; early operator-specific mapping and dispute support will be service-heavy.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: recovered variances or reduced finance review worth at least two monthly fees within six months; prove against historical statements before requesting a long contract.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 8,000-25,000 implementation, then PLN 3,000-15,000 per month plus PLN 0.002-0.01 per processed unit; recovery fees only on contractually accepted adjustments.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Deposit and handling-fee settlements recur monthly at high volume; historical unit-flow baselines and contract rules become embedded.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: cross-operator exception taxonomies and unit-flow benchmarks improve anomaly detection while participant-specific rule maps create durable switching costs
fingerprint.customer: Polish beverage producers, regional grocers, convenience chains, and deposit-system operators participating across more than one operator
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: packaging-compliance advisers, RVM integrators, retail ERP partners, and targeted outreach using a synthetic reconciliation benchmark
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: data-ingestion and reconciliation SaaS plus independent exception review, priced by locations, statements, and processed units
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: producer, retailer, or operator pays when a monthly settlement is certified; an optional success fee applies only to an accepted recovery
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a monthly operator statement or disputed invoice whose unit counts, deposit cash, and handling fees differ across participants

founder_fit: The work is quantitative, anomaly-driven, and suited to automated reconciliation.
Warsaw gives access to Polish scheme stakeholders without requiring a public persona.
A single historical-statement audit can validate value before a large build.
The recurring infrastructure model offers more compounding potential than manual compliance consulting.
risks: Operators may refuse data access or prohibit independent benchmarking.
Unit mismatches can involve fraud allegations and require careful evidentiary controls.
Large retailers and operators may build reconciliation internally.
A success-fee structure can create disputes over attribution and recovered amounts.

structure.control_point: independent variance certificate for deposits, returned units, and handling-fee entitlements
structure.critical_dependency: contractual access to retailer, producer, reverse-vending, logistics, and operator transaction feeds

thesis: Create an independent assurance layer for beverage producers, regional retail chains, and deposit-system operators that reconciles product master data, deposits charged, manual and reverse-vending returns, logistics counts, handling fees, and operator statements. It does not run the deposit system; it produces a defensible variance file before a monthly statement is accepted. The paid event is statement certification or a recovered dispute, with volume pricing aligned to the scheme.
title: Independent Deposit-Return Settlement Auditor
uncertainties: The magnitude of real settlement leakage is not publicly established.
Feed formats, latency, and contractual audit rights across operators are unknown.
It is untested whether producers, retailers, or operators feel the strongest pain and own budget.
Sales cycles with scheme participants may exceed a part-time founder's capacity.
